name: HivePunk 632
subject: Hugging Face dataset-card YAML metadata
thesis: From the claims, dataset-card YAML is a README.md header carrying discovery and provenance metadata (language, license, pretty_name, tags, dataset_info), but the pages read are insufficient to confirm viewer-field behaviour, so any viewer configuration would be unconfirmed.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A repo card is a Markdown file with a YAML block at the beginning and a Markdown body.
claims.quote: The content should be a Markdown file with a YAML block at the beginning and a Markdown body.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The RepoCard example YAML shows language: en and license: mit, returning card data {'language': 'en', 'license': 'mit'}.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The huggingface_hub library provides a Python interface to create, share, and update Model/Dataset Cards.
claims.quote: The huggingface_hub library provides a Python interface to create, share, and update Model/Dataset Cards.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: RepoCard is the parent class of ModelCard, DatasetCard and SpaceCard.
claims.quote: The RepoCard object is the parent class of ModelCard , DatasetCard and SpaceCard .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A dataset card is created by copying a template to a README.md file in the repository.
claims.quote: Create a new dataset card by copying this template to a README.md file in your repository.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: YAML tags from the Datasets Tagging app are pasted at the top of README.md.
claims.quote: Copy the YAML tags under Finalized tag set and paste the tags at the top of your README.md file.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Tags help users discover the dataset on the Hub.
claims.quote: Generate structured tags to help users discover your dataset on the Hub.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The SQuAD example shows pretty_name: SQuAD and language: - en, followed by dataset_info with features and splits.
claims.quote: pretty_name: SQuAD language: - en ... dataset_info: features: - name: id dtype: string

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The features field can explicitly define feature types, useful when type inference is not obvious.
claims.quote: Using the features field you can explicitly define the feature types of your dataset. This is especially useful when type inference is not obvious.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Metadata previously in dataset_infos.json is now deprecated.
claims.quote: These metadata used to be included in the dataset_infos.json file, which is now deprecated.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Because the YAML block is at the beginning of README.md and tags are pasted at the top, tags, language and license are part of the same YAML header.
claims.math: c1 places YAML at beginning; c6 places tags at top of README.md; therefore tags are in the header YAML.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Viewer fields (for example dataset viewer configuration) and their allowed values are not shown in the pages read.
claims.missing: A huggingface.co/docs page explicitly documenting dataset-card viewer YAML fields and allowed values.

risks: The pages read do not list allowed license values or a license vocabulary, so a license string may be unrecognised by the Hub.
The pages read do not list allowed language codes, so language values beyond the en example are not confirmed.
The pages read do not show viewer fields, so viewer configuration cannot be validated from them.
Once filled, the card must be committed to README.md to appear on the repository, so uncommitted YAML changes will not be visible.
dataset_info metadata previously in dataset_infos.json is now deprecated, so relying on the old file format is a risk.
unknowns: Viewer fields (for example dataset viewer configuration) and their allowed values are not shown in the pages read.: A huggingface.co/docs page explicitly documenting dataset-card viewer YAML fields and allowed values.
wouldChangeMind: A huggingface.co/docs page listing viewer fields and their allowed values would remove the UNKNOWN on viewer configuration.
A page listing accepted license and language identifiers would change the risk assessment from unconfirmed to confirmed.
A page showing validation errors for invalid YAML metadata beyond non-dictionary metadata would change the validation risk assessment.
